changes.before:
01 / Research

Two directions, connected.

01 How we deliver software

The Subprime
Code Crisis

What happens across review, testing, security and maintenance when generating code gets easier? This research synthesis studies AI-assisted software delivery as a complete system: verification capacity, code quality, technical debt and long-term ownership, with an inspectable evidence library and adaptable operating protocols.

  • Verification capacity
  • System throughput
  • Long-term ownership
Explore the research ↗

02 What we build

Uncertainty
Architecture

How do we design and operate software whose behavior depends on probabilistic Model Judgment? Uncertainty Architecture develops an engineering vocabulary and draft specification for Thinking Systems, AI control architecture, evaluation, decision authority, runtime control and correction.

  • Model judgment
  • Control architecture
  • Release & runtime evidence
Explore the framework ↗

The repositories hold the living research and its sources. My articles connect the ideas across both directions.
changes.after:
01 / Research

Start with the problem you face.

01 Coding gains without delivery gains

The Subprime
Code Crisis

Code is produced faster, yet work may wait for review, integration or release. My interpretation is that generation, understanding, verification and ownership must be considered together. The Subprime Code Crisis studies that delivery system; it does not assume review is always the constraint.

Evidence and limits: an inspectable research synthesis and source library, with proposed operating protocols. Evidence differs across tasks and settings; neither more code nor this synthesis proves a universal productivity effect.

  • Verification capacity
  • System throughput
  • Long-term ownership
Explore the research ↗

Start with verification and delivery-cost reading →

02 Consequential actions under model judgment

Uncertainty
Architecture

An agent can propose a plausible action while its authority, evidence or recovery path remains unclear. Uncertainty Architecture studies the software system and its wider control perimeter: human roles, operating limits, evidence, decision authority and correction.

Evidence and limits: early-stage conceptual research and a draft engineering specification, not an accepted standard or a demonstrated guarantee of safe operation. Current meanings belong to the living specification.

  • Model judgment
  • Control architecture
  • Release & runtime evidence
Explore the framework ↗

Start with Thinking Systems and control reading →

The repositories are the living sources. Articles are dated author perspectives; their claims and proposed practices need assessment in context.

      and more than 120 engineers. That experience shapes my research into software delivery
      and systems that depend on model judgment.

text.T003:
What happens when machines generate faster than people can understand and verify? And what
      changes when the software itself relies on model judgment?
text.T007:
I see the AI-assisted SDLC as structurally unbalanced where generation accelerates faster
        than human understanding, verification and ownership. More output can coexist with review
        queues, rework and fragile maintenance.
text.T009:
investigates this gap and how teams can rebalance
        generation, verification and ownership. It treats proposed responses as hypotheses to test
        in context.
text.T019:
studies what I call Thinking Systems: software in
        which consequential runtime responsibilities depend partly on probabilistic model judgment.
        This is where I see the fullest expression of today's AI potential — and some of its hardest
        engineering problems.
text.T020:
The controlled object is the software system. Its control perimeter also includes human
        roles, evidence, decision authority and corrective action. It needs development lifecycles
        and operating models suited to uncertainty. Much remains to develop and test.

text.T002: Two engineering problems. Two starting points.
text.T003: For delivery leaders: where did the coding gains go? For architects and AI teams: what may a system decide and do, and what happens when it is wrong?
text.T007: When more generated code meets longer review queues, rework or fragile maintenance, examine the whole flow before assuming which step is the constraint.

delivery.when: Read this when faster generation leaves questions about verification and human understanding. The author’s argument connects code output with responsibility for checking it.
Read this when coding-tool savings are being treated as a reason to reduce engineering capacity. A critical author perspective on shifted costs, not a validated ROI model.

systems.when: Read this when a product relies on consequential model judgment and you need to distinguish the software from its wider control perimeter. A conceptual starting point, not production assurance.

Read this for the December 2025 control-theory perspective on AI governance. Its human-only controller examples are historical; use the living Uncertainty Architecture specification for current meanings.

leadership.when: Read this when deciding whether PMO roles and metrics help delivery or add overhead. A practitioner view of contextual operating choices.
Read this when exploring roles and communication across human and AI work. The organizational model is a preliminary example, not a confirmed implementation result.
